stem.en: Chlorine steals an electron from sodium but shares one with another chlorine. Kabir says chlorine "changes its mind". What actually decides?

text.en: The difference in pull. Chlorine pulls far harder than sodium, so it takes. Two chlorines pull equally, so neither can take, and they share.
How many electrons chlorine has that day.

feedback.en: Chlorine always has seven outer electrons. What changes is the other atom.

text.en: Whether it is a solid or a gas.

feedback.en: Chlorine gas shares with itself. Chlorine in salt steals. The state is a result, not a cause.

text.en: Chlorine prefers sharing and only steals when forced.

feedback.en: Atoms have no preferences. The knot ends up wherever the two pulls put it, and that is the whole rule.

explanation.en: One atom, two partners, two different grips. The atom did not change. The difference in pull between it and its partner did.
